messages:
alex: Anyone seeing a spike in pending gangs in apse1? noticed a bunch of tiny-gang pods stuck waiting for warmnode coalesce.
maria: yep, saw it ~13:02 UTC. warmpool instances not releasing slots, lots of tiny-gang pods Pending.
jun: scheduler logs showing repeated lease commit timeouts for the warmnode coalescer:
```
E0503 13:02:10 scheduler.go:234] coalesce: lease commit timeout for warmnode=w-n-23, err=kvcache.stale
E0503 13:02:11 scheduler.go:234] coalesce: lease commit timeout for warmnode=w-n-24
```
alex: is this related to the lease-timeout tweak we rolled last week? we bumped commit timeout down to 30s on the canary.
ops-jen: I can take w-n-23 out of rotation and restart the coalescer agent. will that kill in-flight tiny-gangs? any objections?
maria: draining will evict the tiny-gang pods — they should reschedule but may get preempted. low user impact, fine during the window :thumbsup:
jun: alternative quick fix is a scheduler patch to treat stale warmnode leases as reclaimable after 45s (PR #1209 ready). but that's a risky change during peak.
alex: agree, avoid scheduler change mid-day. ops-jen, please drain w-n-23 and restart. capture logs and we can triage.
ops-jen: starting drain now:
```
$ kubectl drain w-n-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
node/w-n-23 cordoned
evicting pod tiny-gang-abcde
```
ops-jen: restart coalescer agent on w-n-23 -> done, watching slots free up.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-20230503-42 assigned: eng-platform severity: low — alert(rule/pending_gang_rate) triggered :rotating_light:
maria: looks good — warmpool freed 8 slots after restart, pending gangs started to schedule again. keeping an eye for 10m.
jun: I'll open a postmortem and bisect the lease commit change; noting suspect: kvcache TTL interaction under high attach churn.
alex: follow-ups: add metric coalesce.commit.latency and alert if p95 > 25s. add runbook step: if >5 pending-gangs for >5m, drain implicated warmnode and restart coalescer.
ops-jen: noted, will update runbook and postmortem with commands and telemetry links.
alex: thanks everyone — keeping this thread pinned until postmortem published.
